case_title: Anokhilal v. State of Madhya Pradesh
previous_criminal_record: Yes - earlier conviction (judgment dated 21.10.2010) for committing carnal sex with a small boy
evidence_type: Circumstantial (last-seen evidence), eyewitness-type last-seen testimony of Kirti Bai, DNA and forensic (FSL) reports, injury evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Victim a nine-year-old girl; brutal rape; throttling; body dumped in a field; accused exploited the victim's trust; prior conviction for a sexual offence (as noted by the High Court)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC ss.363, 366, 377, 376(2)(f) and 302 r/w POCSO s.6; death sentence (s.302); seven years RI each for ss.363, 366, 377; life imprisonment (s.376(2)(f)); fine Rs.1000 each
high_court_outcome: Death sentence confirmed and other sentences upheld; appeal (Criminal Appeal No.748 of 2013) dismissed and reference (No.4 of 2013) answered in favour of confirmation
neutral_facts: A nine-year-old girl was reported missing in the evening of 30 January 2013 after a neighbour of her family had sent her to buy a bidi from a shop; she did not return. Her body was found in an open field the next day. The investigation recovered hairs from the victim's fist and skin from under her fingernails, which were reported to belong to the accused. Semen found on the victim's pyjamas was reported to be the accused's, and blood found on the accused's underwear was reported to be the victim's. The victim's body bore numerous injuries and marks of throttling, and she had been sexually assaulted. A witness, Kirti Bai, stated that the victim was seen alive with the accused at a time close to the incident. After the incident the accused was not seen, and he was arrested on 4 February 2013. Investigation was completed and a charge-sheet was filed, and the case proceeded on the basis of this evidence.
physical_harm: Death of the victim by throttling; rape and carnal sex; numerous injuries on the body
premeditation_planning: Found by the High Court (not decided by the Supreme Court): accused followed the victim with a premeditated mind
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court made no finding on the merits of the evidence; it noted that the DNA report formed the foundation of the High Court's discussion and that the High Court relied on last-seen evidence and DNA/FSL reports
post_offence_conduct: Absconded after the incident (as noted by the High Court)
custody_duration: In detention since 04.02.2013; total duration not stated
trial_duration: offence: 30.01.2013 (missing report lodged; trial court notes incident occurred midnight 30-31 January); trial judgment: 04.03.2013; High Court: 27.06.2013; Supreme Court: 18.12.2019
legal_representation: Appellant: Sidharth Luthra, Senior Advocate (for the Supreme Court Legal Services Authority), with Amicus Curiae; State: Varun Chopra, Deputy Advocate General
investigation_status: FIR registered 30.01.2013; body found 01.02.2013; accused arrested 04.02.2013; charge-sheet filed 13.02.2013; charges framed 19.02.2013; trial concluded 04.03.2013
procedural_irregularity: Amicus Curiae appointed on the same day charges were framed, with no time to study the record or meet the accused; 13 witnesses examined within seven days; accused examined under s.313 CrPC before complete evidence; trial concluded within a fortnight without awaiting FSL/DNA reports
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted, death sentence (04.03.2013). High Court: death sentence and other sentences upheld; appeal dismissed (27.06.2013). Supreme Court: convictions and sentences set aside; de novo consideration directed
prosecution_argument: The evidence pointed to the accused's guilt without doubt, so the conviction recorded by the courts below was correct and called for no interference
defence_argument: Amicus Curiae was appointed on the day charges were framed, with no sufficient opportunity to study the matter or interact with the accused; the trial was unfair and prejudicial
legal_principle_applied: Right to free legal aid under Art. 39-A and Art. 21 requires real and meaningful assistance, with counsel given sufficient time to prepare; expeditious trial must not compromise fairness
precedent_relied_upon: Bashira v. State of U.P., [1969] 1 SCR 32 (relied on); Mohd. Hussain alias Julfikar Ali v. State (NCT of Delhi), (2012) 9 SCC 408; Hussainara Khatoon (IV), (1980) 1 SCC 98; Ambadas Laxman Shinde (2018) 18 SCC 788; Imtiyaz Ramzan Khan (2018) 9 SCC 160; V.K. Sasikala (2012) 9 SCC 771 (referred to)
other_sentence_order: De novo consideration by the Trial Court; counsel may address whether charges should be amended, whether prosecution witnesses should be recalled, and whether expert evidence is needed on FSL and DNA reports; matter listed on 18.02.2020 for other related issues
